narrative:
The model predicts an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart in the near future.

Three factors stood out most in driving this prediction. First, having received other job opportunities while at your current company was the strongest influence, pushing the model strongly toward expecting you to leave. Second, your overall career experience of 6-10 years also pulled the prediction toward leaving; while this is fairly common among employees the model expects to stay (35% of them), it still contributed noticeably. Third, your 1-5 years with this organization added further weight toward departure, a tenure shared by about half of those predicted to stay.

These elements together created a picture of someone who is marketable and has built enough broad experience to make a move attractive. Although many of your other experiences, such as feeling recognized, having medical insurance, and reporting medium work-life balance, would normally encourage staying, they were not strong enough to outweigh the top three signals.

Your organization should discuss retention options with you, such as clearer advancement paths or new challenges. You may want to reflect on whether those external opportunities better match your goals. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook. (218 words)
